candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — aseptic technique and catheter infection prevention
candidate.educational_objective: Apply CDC central-line dressing-change principles: hand hygiene, aseptic technique, appropriate skin antisepsis, a sterile dressing, and either clean or sterile gloves; distinguish routine maintenance from insertion-level maximal sterile barriers.

options.A: Perform hand hygiene, maintain aseptic technique, prepare the site with greater than 0.5% chlorhexidine with alcohol unless contraindicated, and apply a sterile dressing; clean or sterile gloves are acceptable for the dressing change.
options.B: Use sterile gloves, but omit skin antisepsis when the previous transparent dressing remained intact.
options.C: Use clean technique without aseptic precautions once a central catheter has remained complication-free for several days.
options.D: Use maximal sterile barrier precautions with cap, mask, sterile gown, sterile gloves, and a full-body drape because routine dressing changes should mirror central-line insertion.

candidate.rationale: CDC guidance recommends hand hygiene before and after dressing an intravascular catheter and maintenance of aseptic technique during catheter care. For central venous catheter dressing changes, clean skin should be prepared with a greater-than-0.5% chlorhexidine preparation with alcohol unless chlorhexidine is contraindicated, in which case listed alternatives may be used. Either clean or sterile gloves may be worn for dressing changes, and the site should be covered with a sterile gauze or sterile transparent semipermeable dressing. Maximal sterile barrier precautions are recommended for CVC/PICC insertion or guidewire exchange, not every routine dressing change.
candidate.source_claim_supported: CDC directs hand hygiene before/after catheter dressing and aseptic technique for catheter care; either clean or sterile gloves are acceptable for dressing changes. For central venous catheter dressing changes, greater than 0.5% chlorhexidine with alcohol is recommended unless contraindicated, and the site is covered with a sterile gauze or sterile transparent semipermeable dressing. Maximal sterile barriers are specified for CVC/PICC insertion or guidewire exchange.
